---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Cash-Earnings Intangible Conservatism
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ni), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible-intensive firms with sustained cash profitability and cash flow exceeding accounting earnings earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Expensed intangible investment can depress accounting earnings even when the firm is generating cash, so the cash-minus-earnings spread is a conservatism channel rather than a simple profitability level. Requiring both cash profitability and cumulative R&D/advertising intensity helps distinguish productive internally generated intangibles from accrual-heavy profitability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Intangible Harvest Operating Leverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at), 1)), MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with prior intangible investment, improving operating margins, and easing intangible expense intensity are entering a profitable harvest phase.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This tests whether past R&D and advertising are beginning to scale, rather than simply rewarding current high spending. The margin-trend leg validates productivity, while the declining spending-intensity trend captures operating leverage from previously built intangible assets.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Scalable Intangible Sales Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(sale, at), RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible-intensive firms that also generate high sales per reported asset and strong operating margins are underpriced because book assets understate scalable productive capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The signal combines margin validation with an asset-light scale channel, so it is not merely a profitability-by-intangible-intensity double sort. High sales-to-assets among cumulative R&D/advertising investors is consistent with unrecognized intangible capital supporting revenue without appearing fully on the balance sheet.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Internal Intangibles over Goodwill Profit
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 5), at), RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitable firms with internally built intangible investment rather than acquisition goodwill earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Internally generated R&D and advertising are more likely to be understated by accounting, while goodwill may reflect acquisition premia already paid. The interaction rewards profitability when it is paired with internal intangible formation and penalizes goodwill-heavy profitability that is less clearly an underrecognized productive asset base.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Brand-Customer Margin Inflection
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 1), 1)), IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xad, 0), 3), COALESCE(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 0)), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with brand or customer-related intangible assets followed by improving operating margins earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This shifts the brand/customer mechanism from contemporaneous growth to a lagged payoff test: prior advertising and identifiable non-goodwill intangibles should later appear in margins. It avoids the prior weakest-link problem by using a continuous interaction rather than forcing firms with missing advertising into an arbitrary minimum bucket.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Financing-Resilient Intangible Profit
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, ADD(dp, COALESCE(xint, 0))), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible-intensive firms that remain profitable after depreciation and financing costs earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This validation leg asks whether intangible investment is supported by a durable residual operating surplus, not just EBITDA before capital and financing charges. Pairing that residual profitability with recent R&D and advertising intensity targets firms whose intangible investment appears economically productive rather than speculative or debt-dependent.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Cash-Earnings Intangible Conservatism---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Two of the three legs reproduce the archived "Cash-Funded Intangible Compounder" almost verbatim, and the only new leg — (oancf − ni)/at — is the classic Sloan (1996) accruals anomaly, so this is a known-anomaly bolt-on to an existing signal rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Intangible Harvest Operating Leverage---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The declining-spend-intensity trend leg is a genuinely different economic idea (harvest/operating-leverage phase) rather than a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived margin-inflection signal, though the level leg (high intangible intensity) and the trend leg (falling intangible intensity) partially offset each other and the triple-rank product risks thin, unstable extreme buckets.

---CRITIQUE Scalable Intangible Sales Profitability---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: By the DuPont identity margin × turnover ≈ oibdp/at, so despite the stated claim to the contrary this collapses to essentially operating profitability × cumulative intangible intensity — i.e., the archived "Capitalized Intangible Yield x Intensity" construction in disguise.

---CRITIQUE Internal Intangibles over Goodwill Profit---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The internally-generated-minus-acquired intangible differencing is a substantively new distinction (not just another profitability × R&D-intensity double sort), though subtracting a goodwill stock from a five-year expense flow is dimensionally awkward and the profitability leg remains heavily overlapped with the archive.

---CRITIQUE Brand-Customer Margin Inflection---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Structurally this is the archived "Lagged Intangible Margin Inflection" with only the intangible proxy swapped (xad + non-goodwill intan for xrd + xad), and the stated rationale is internally inconsistent since COALESCE(xad,0) still stacks all non-advertisers at the bottom of the rank rather than avoiding the arbitrary-bucket problem.

---CRITIQUE Financing-Resilient Intangible Profit---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: oibdp − dp − xint is just a near-pretax-income numerator, so this is the fourth profitability-level × intangible-intensity double sort in the archive with a cosmetically different profitability definition and no new economic channel.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Cash Payoff to Intangible Ramp
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(ADD(MA(RATIO(oancf, sale), 3), ACCEL(RATIO(oancf, sale))), 1)), IND_RANK(LAG(TREND(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with prior increases in intangible investment intensity and subsequently strong or improving cash margins earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces the cash-profitability plus accruals construction with a payoff-timing mechanism: intangible spending is useful when a prior ramp is followed by cash-margin validation. The signal avoids the Sloan accruals leg and is not just current cash profitability multiplied by intangible intensity.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Gross-to-Operating Intangible Conversion
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(oibdp, SUB(revt, cogs)), 3), 1)), IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3), sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose prior intangible investment is followed by better conversion of gross profit into operating profit earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This avoids the DuPont margin-times-turnover collapse by measuring operating drop-through from gross profit rather than asset turnover. The interaction tests whether R&D and advertising create scalable products or brands whose gross profits increasingly survive operating-expense absorption.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Goodwill-Light Intangible Cash High
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, sale), 3), 5)), IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(COALESCE(SUB(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), 0), at), RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with identifiable non-goodwill intangible assets and cash margins near their own historical highs earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This removes the zero-advertising weakest-link problem by relying on recognized non-goodwill intangibles rather than advertising availability. The profitability validation comes from a firm-specific cash-margin high, while the intangible leg distinguishes productive identifiable intangibles from goodwill-heavy acquisition accounting.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Debt-Light Self-Funded Intangible Ramp
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, ADD(at, TS_SUM(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), 3)))), MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xint, 0), sale), 3)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms ramping intangible investment while generating operating cash flow and reducing interest burden are more likely to have validated, internally funded intangible productivity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This revises the near-pretax-income double sort into a financing-resilience mechanism: intangible expansion is most valuable when it is not accompanied by rising debt-service pressure. The cash-flow leg validates self-funding capacity, while the interest-trend leg filters out firms whose intangible investment depends on increasingly costly financing.
